newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka's Hayleys Ltd sticks to formula.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka's Hayleys Ltd sticks to formula.

text.p: Sri Lankan blue chip Hayleys Ltd, which saw a substantial rise in profits in the financial year to the end of March, expects to stay with its tried and tested growth formula of adding value to local raw materials.

The conglomerate that consolidates accounts with 65 units, eight of which are listed, said net profit after tax rose by 32.5 percent to 283 million rupees ($4.87 million) led by improved income from adding value to rubber, coir and coconut shell charcoal.
Market analysts said on Wednesday they were upgrading Hayleys to a buy since results were higher than expected.

Panduka Ambanpola, head of research at Jardine Fleming HNB Stock Brokers, told Reuters that he was upgrading Hayleys to a buy from a hold since profits were beyond an expected 233 million rupees. "Profits for the current 1997/98 financial year should be at least 352 million and we are, therefore, upgrading the share to a buy from a hold," said Dushyanth Wijayasinha, analyst at Asia Capital.

"Since the 1970s Hayleys has grown by adding value to local raw materials, where the return on capital employed is better than in agriculture, tourism or services," Sunil Mendis, chairman and chief executive of Hayleys told Reuters.
Dipped Products Ltd, a joint venture with Richard Pieris & Co, where net profit rose by 124 percent to 205.13 million rupees, manufactures rubber gloves for export and manages plantations.
"Haycarb, which turns coconut shell charcoal into activated carbon at two factories in Sri Lanka and one in Thailand, also performed well," said Mendis.
Activated carbon chips and pellets are widely used in the gold mining industry and to purify water and treat effluent.

Three unlisted units -- Ravi Industries, Rileys Ltd and Toyo Cushion Lanka (Pvt) Ltd -- which are all 100 percent export-oriented ventures, contributed substantially to the group's bottom line, Mendis said.

Ravi manufactures and exports household and industrial coir brushes. Rileys Ltd exports cleaning devices manufactured from natural and synthetic raw material while Toyo Cushions exports rubberised coir used for bedding, upholstery and horticulture.
Hayleys, despite its penchant for industries that add value to local raw materials, says it has also gone into agriculture.
"We began by growing gherkins for export, but had to soon start adding value to compete with India," Mendis said.

Simply exporting gherkins in brine in bulk was unprofitable after India, a major exporter, steadily devalued its currency over a five- to six-year period. The Sri Lankan rupee fell only by about 50 percent in the same period.
Hayleys now exports bottled pickled and garnished gherkins and silver skin onions.
